Debugger workflow to pull secrets from a service binary.

name: Thick Client - Static/Dynamic Analysis
description: Analyze a desktop client to find secrets and logic flaws: ProcMon watches file/registry/process behavior, dnSpy/de4dot decompile .NET, x64dbg debugs native code, strings pulls embedded artifacts (URLs, creds, base64 blobs).

defense.why_it_works: Thick clients often embed database connection strings, API keys, and credentials in plaintext within binary files or construct them at runtime. GDB breakpoints at connection functions (e.g., SQLDriverConnect) capture fully assembled plaintext credentials from CPU registers before they are used.
defense.prerequisites: Access to the thick client binary. Ability to run analysis tools (strings, GDB, ProcMon). No anti-debug protection on the application.
defense.impact: Credential extraction (database passwords, API tokens, service account credentials) granting access to backend systems with privileges higher than the client's intended access.
defense.detection: Unusual tool execution (strings64.exe, GDB, de4dot, dnSpy) on application directories. Debugger processes attached to the application. Memory-scanning processes.
defense.artifacts: Process audit log (debugger attached to application) | File system access log (strings tool reading binary) | DLL / config file access events
defense.prevention: Never store credentials in thick client binaries. Use OS credential stores (DPAPI, Keychain). Require the client to authenticate to a backend API that holds secrets -- never expose DB credentials to the client.
defense.misconfiguration: Thick client embeds database connection string with plaintext password in the binary. Application connects directly to DB rather than through a backend API.
defense.evasion: Analyze the client offline (decompile/traffic capture) so no attack traffic hits the server until you have the exploit ready.
